tests.name: Headers and Body for Every File
tests.description: Requests each of the 11 files over a raw socket. Checks the status line, the Content-Type and Content-Length headers, CRLF line endings, a body identical to the file, and that the server closes the connection.

tests.name: 404 for Missing Resources
tests.description: A missing file, a missing directory, a path below a regular file (stat fails with ENOTDIR) and a name with no extension all get 'HTTP/1.0 404 Not Found' with Content-Length 0 and no body. The server keeps serving.

tests.name: Request Sent in Small Pieces
tests.description: The client sends its request one byte at a time, then seven bytes at a time with 50 ms pauses. A server that answers after a single read() sees only part of the request line.

tests.name: End of Request Straddles a Read Boundary
tests.description: Requests padded with a long header so the closing CRLF CRLF starts at byte 510, 511, 1022, 4094, 4095 or 8190 (split across two reads of 512, 1024, 4096 or 8192 bytes), and one with 64 KiB of headers. The server must consume the whole request and find the marker across the split.

tests.name: Connection Queue Unit Tests
tests.description: Builds resources/queue_test.c against connection_queue.c: FIFO order across wraparound, enqueue blocking on a full queue and dequeue on an empty one, shutdown waking every blocked thread, dequeues draining the queue after shutdown (as the spec says), enqueue failing after shutdown, and two stress runs: 4 producers with 4 consumers, and 1 producer with 8 mostly waiting consumers, where a woken consumer often finds its element already taken (while, not if, around the wait). Any element dequeued twice, or a -1 before shutdown (a worker would quit), stops the run.

tests.name: Connection Queue Unit Tests Under ThreadSanitizer
tests.description: The same unit tests built with -fsanitize=thread: no data races reported.

tests.name: Fixed Pool of Five Worker Threads
tests.description: Counts the server's threads in /proc: the main thread plus 5 workers before any client, after 100 sequential requests and after 20 concurrent ones. A thread per connection, or threads that exit, change the count. Also reads each thread's blocked-signal mask: the spec has every worker block all signals, so SIGINT can only go to main.

tests.name: Forty Concurrent Clients
tests.description: 40 curl downloads at once: 5 in the workers, 5 in the queue, and the rest waiting in the listen backlog while the main thread blocks on the full queue. All 40 files arrive intact.

tests.name: Five Rounds Through the concurrent_open Barrier
tests.description: Like provided test 2 (LD_PRELOAD=./concurrent_open.so) but with 25 requests, so every one of five rounds needs all 5 workers inside open() at the same time.

tests.name: SIGINT With No Clients
tests.description: SIGINT reaches a server blocked in accept() with idle workers. It exits within 3 s, with status 0 and no output.

tests.name: SIGINT Drains the Queue
tests.description: Five slow clients occupy every worker (they send their request after 2.5 s), three more wait in the queue, then SIGINT. The spec lets dequeues continue until the queue is empty, so all 8 clients get complete responses before the server exits with status 0.

tests.name: SIGINT While the Main Thread Waits on a Full Queue
tests.description: Five slow clients occupy the workers, five more fill the queue, and an eleventh leaves the main thread blocked in enqueue when SIGINT arrives. Nothing deadlocks: all 11 clients are served once the slow ones send their requests, and the server exits with status 0.

tests.name: Clients That Misbehave
tests.description: One client connects and closes, one sends half a request and closes, one sends a malformed request line. The server may report them (its output isn't checked here) but must close those connections, keep serving and exit cleanly.

tests.name: Clients That Abandon a Download (SIGPIPE)
tests.description: Runs the server with SIGPIPE at its default action, as from a terminal (testius itself ignores SIGPIPE), under LD_PRELOAD=./concurrent_open.so. Five clients abandon a 32 MiB download after 64 KiB. The first write() after that fails with ECONNRESET; a server that keeps writing gets SIGPIPE on the next one, which kills the whole process unless the worker blocks it, as the spec has every worker do. Five concurrent requests afterwards prove all 5 workers survived. Server output isn't checked.

tests.name: 1500 Sequential Requests
tests.description: 1500 requests (1375 files, 125 missing) against the 1024-descriptor limit: a client socket or file left open per request makes accept() or open() fail partway. The number of open descriptors afterwards must equal the number before.

tests.name: Port Already in Use
tests.description: A second server on the same port fails at bind(): it exits promptly with a nonzero status and says 'Address already in use' (perror's wording). The first server keeps working.

tests.name: No Valgrind Errors or Leaks
tests.description: The server under valgrind with testius's options serves 15 concurrent downloads, a 404 and the misbehaving clients, then gets SIGINT: no errors, and every block freed (workers joined, addrinfo freed).

tests.name: No ThreadSanitizer Warnings
tests.description: http_server_tsan serves 40 concurrent downloads, a 404 and the misbehaving clients, then gets SIGINT. The spec says TSAN may be a hidden test: no data races reported, exit status 0.
